blocks.orig: We might be a bit prejudiced, but in our opinion, Tanzanian people are the best. Many of our clients love their guide(s) and speak highly of the staff they encounter in the lodges during their trip. People are friendly, funny, open, warm-hearted and very helpful. So when going on safari, you might want to tip the people you encounter. The question is; how much to give?
blocks.html: Perhaps we are a little biased, but we think Tanzanians are the best people you could meet. Our clients often grow fond of their guide(s) and have nothing but praise for the staff they meet in the lodges along the way. They are friendly, funny, open, warm-hearted and always ready to help. So on safari you will probably want to tip the people who look after you. The only question is: how much?

blocks.orig: Usually, smaller tips are used for people working in the accommodations where you spend the night. You might want to tip the people carrying your luggage upon arrival, or that really cool waiter in the restaurant. Giving these people a small tip is very common, and amounts of 1 – 5 USD per person or 2,000 to 10,000 Tanzanian shilling are much appreciated.
blocks.html: Smaller tips are normally reserved for the staff at the accommodation where you are staying overnight. Think of the person who carries your bags when you arrive, or that great waiter in the restaurant. Tipping them a little is entirely normal, and something in the region of 1 – 5 USD per person, or 2,000 to 10,000 Tanzanian shilling, is always welcome.

blocks.orig: It is also possible to leave a tip for the entire staff since most accommodations have a tipping box at the reception. Amounts of 5 – 10 USD or 10,000 – 20,000 Tanzanian shillings per night are very reasonable for that.
blocks.html: Another option is to leave something for everyone who works there: at most places you will find a box for this at reception. Putting in 5 – 10 USD, or 10,000 – 20,000 Tanzanian shillings, for each night you stay is perfectly reasonable.

blocks.orig: For this purpose, it’s good to carry some dollar notes or Tanzanian shilling bills.
blocks.html: It helps to have a few dollar notes or Tanzanian shilling bills on you for exactly this reason.

blocks.orig: We highly appreciate it if you also tip your guide (and driver, if applicable) at the end of the safari. As a general guideline, we advise you to give 10 USD per day per person in your group, for the duration of the safari.
blocks.html: It would also mean a lot to us if you rewarded your guide (plus the driver, where there is one) when the trip comes to an end. Our rule of thumb: 10 USD a day from each member of your party, for every day you are out on safari.

blocks.orig: This means that if you are with 4 people going on a multiple-day safari, this can add up to several hundred dollars for one driver/guide. That sounds like a lot of money, but keep in mind that your guide accompanies you day and night, and takes care of all your needs during the safari.
blocks.html: For a party of 4 on a safari lasting several days, that can come to a few hundred dollars for a single driver/guide. It may sound like a great deal, but remember that your guide is with you around the clock and looks after everything you need throughout the safari.

blocks.orig: When climbing Mount Kilimanjaro, you have a team of guides, porters and cooks accompanying you. Tips represent excellent motivation, as it is a nice add-on to the team member’s income. And since they stay with you day and night for the duration of your climb, it also shows your appreciation for the good care they took of you on the mountain.
blocks.html: On a Kilimanjaro climb you are supported by a whole team of guides, porters and cooks. Tips are a strong motivator, because they are a welcome supplement to each team member's income. And as they are at your side day and night for the entire climb, a tip is also a way of thanking them for looking after you so well on the mountain.

blocks.orig: A group of climbers usually gives 15 USD per day to the lead guide, 10 USD per day to the assistant guide, 10 USD per day to the cook, and 8 USD per day per porter, for the duration of the climb.
blocks.html: The customary amounts from a climbing party, for every day on the mountain, are 15 USD daily for the lead guide, 10 USD daily for the assistant guide, 10 USD daily for the cook and 8 USD daily for each porter.

blocks.orig: Please keep in mind that climbs require 8 (for 1 climber) to 48 (12 climbers) staff members. This means tipping amounts add up to well over 400 USD for the duration of the climb. Again, this seems a lot but keep in mind that they guide you up the mountain, monitor your health, carry all your luggage and cook you the most amazing food in difficult circumstances.
blocks.html: Bear in mind that a climb needs anywhere from 8 (for 1 climber) to 48 (12 climbers) staff members, so the total in tips easily passes 400 USD over the course of the climb. Once more, that looks like a lot, but these are the people who lead you up the mountain, keep an eye on your health, carry all your gear and cook you wonderful food in tough conditions.

blocks.orig: We trust that your safari or climb was so amazing, that you happily tip your guide or porters at the end. But also know; you never have to feel obligated!
blocks.html: We hope your safari or climb turns out to be so good that tipping your guide or porters at the end feels like the natural thing to do. That said, you should never feel you are obliged to!

blocks.orig: At the end of the day, our guides earn decent salaries and these tips are welcome extras. As there is still quite some poverty and little to no social security in Tanzania, they often serve as savings or to support the extended family.
blocks.html: In the end, our guides are paid a decent wage, and tips are a welcome bonus on top. Because poverty is still widespread in Tanzania and there is little or no social security, that money frequently goes into savings or towards supporting the wider family.
